title: Tensor colimits with independent site and coefficient universes
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a site essentially small in a coefficient universe $w$, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings in that universe, and let $M$ be a sheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The functor $N\mapsto M\otimes_R N$, with the sheafified sectionwise tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], preserves colimits of every diagram whose object and morphism types lie in universe $w$. The object and morphism universes of the site may differ from $w$.

proof.text: Let a be module sheafification and let epsilon be its invertible counit on sheaves [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The monoidal tensorator and epsilon_M give a natural isomorphism a followed by tensorLeft M with presheaf tensorLeft M.val followed by a. This is the explicit composition of the mapped counit and Functor.Monoidal.commTensorLeft.

The presheaf tensor functor preserves coefficient-sized colimits by Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf.Monoidal, lines 237-241; sheafification preserves them as a left adjoint. Therefore their composite, and the naturally isomorphic precomposition of tensorLeft M with a, preserve them.

Apply CategoryTheory.Adjunction.preservesColimitsOfSize_iff in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.FullyFaithfulLimits, lines 56-62, to the reflective sheafification adjunction. Its right adjoint is fully faithful, so preservation after precomposition with a implies preservation by tensorLeft M.

As a shared proved corollary, tensorLeft_additive_independent shrinks tensor colimit preservation to finite diagrams, obtains binary biproduct preservation from binary coproduct preservation, and applies Functor.additive_of_preservesBinaryBiproducts. The independent-coefficient zero-morphism theorem supplies its zero preservation. The parent cone proof and bounded-flat criterion import and reuse this one declaration instead of separately proving identical private lemmas.

The shared explicit site tensor comparisons siteTensorRightIso, tensorRightPresentation and siteSheafTensorRightIso identify the sectionwise construction, its sheafification, and tensorRight using identities on tensor generators and the monoidal sheafification counit. Both the parent cone proof and bounded-flat criterion reuse these single constructions.
